How to calculate income tax in Norway (2026)

Norway taxes salary in three layers: 22% on ordinary income after allowances, a stepped bracket tax (trinnskatt) on gross pay, and 7.6% national insurance. On NOK 750,000 a resident pays about NOK 197,000 in total and keeps about NOK 553,000 (73.7%). Foreign workers who qualify can choose the PAYE scheme instead, a flat 25% of gross, which leaves NOK 450,000 on NOK 600,000.

What the law says

The figures below are the 2026 rates as the calculator models them, in Norwegian kroner (NOK). The calculator uses the standard national rates. It does not model the lower rates that apply in Finnmark and northern Troms, and it ignores any municipality-specific items. Your tax is based on residency, not on your visa or passport.

Ordinary income tax (22%)

Ordinary income is taxed at a flat 22%. Before the rate applies, the calculator takes off two things: the minimum standard deduction (46% of gross pay, capped at NOK 95,700) and a personal allowance of NOK 114,540. For most salaries the cap bites, so about NOK 210,240 is taken off before the 22%.

Bracket tax (trinnskatt)

Bracket tax is charged on gross personal income, with no deductions, in steps. Only the part of your pay inside each band is taxed at that band's rate.

Gross incomeRate
NOK 0 to NOK 226,1000%
NOK 226,101 to NOK 318,3001.7%
NOK 318,301 to NOK 725,0504.0%
NOK 725,051 to NOK 980,10013.7%
NOK 980,101 to NOK 1,467,20016.8%
Over NOK 1,467,20017.8%

National insurance (7.6%)

Employees pay national insurance (trygdeavgift) of 7.6% of gross pay. It starts above NOK 99,650 and phases in at 25% of the amount above that threshold until the full 7.6% applies. The calculator applies this to salary income.

The PAYE scheme for foreign workers

The PAYE scheme (PAYE-ordningen) is a simplified regime for foreign workers who meet the conditions set by the Norwegian Tax Administration. It replaces ordinary tax, bracket tax and national insurance with a flat 25% of gross pay, and it has no deductions. The calculator allows it for pay up to NOK 725,050 a year. It also has a switch for people who stay outside Norwegian national insurance, which lowers the flat rate to 17.4%. Check eligibility with Skatteetaten before choosing it.

Tax card and withholding

Your employer withholds tax using your tax card (skattekort), which you get through Skatteetaten. Tax is withheld over ten and a half months, so December pay carries half the usual deduction and you see a larger payslip before Christmas. The final bill is settled in the tax return you file the following spring.

Sources

  • Skatteetaten (Norwegian Tax Administration), rates, tax card, the PAYE scheme for foreign workers
  • NAV, national insurance, membership of the National Insurance Scheme
  • UDI, Norwegian Directorate of Immigration, visas and residence permits for workers

Worked examples

Rules for 2026. Every amount below is worked out by the calculator's own engine, the same one the tool runs.

  • How much tax do you pay in Norway on NOK 750,000?
  • Norway PAYE scheme: take-home pay on NOK 600,000 at a flat 25%

How much tax do you pay in Norway on NOK 750,000?

This is a resident on ordinary tax with a NOK 750,000 salary. The minimum standard deduction hits its NOK 95,700 cap and the personal allowance adds NOK 114,540, so NOK 539,760 is taxed at 22%, giving NOK 118,747. Bracket tax on the full NOK 750,000 adds NOK 21,256, because the top NOK 24,950 sits in the 13.7% band. National insurance of 7.6% takes NOK 57,000. You keep about NOK 552,997, or 73.7% of gross.

  1. Gross paya year, before taxNOK 750,000
  2. Minimum standard deduction and personal allowancelowers the taxable incomeNOK 210,240
  3. Tax on ordinary income (22%)tax, taken from pay−NOK 118,747
  4. Bracket tax (trinnskatt)tax, taken from pay−NOK 21,256
  5. NOK 0 to NOK 226,100 at 0%bracket, part of the tax aboveNOK 0
  6. NOK 226,100 to NOK 318,300 at 1.7%bracket, part of the tax aboveNOK 1,567
  7. NOK 318,300 to NOK 725,050 at 4%bracket, part of the tax aboveNOK 16,270
  8. NOK 725,050 to NOK 750,000 at 13.7%bracket, part of the tax aboveNOK 3,418
  9. National insurance (7.6%)contribution, taken from pay−NOK 57,000
  10. Take-home pay73.7% of gross, NOK 46,083 a monthNOK 552,997

Your marginal rate is 43.3%: 22% ordinary tax, 13.7% bracket tax and 7.6% national insurance. Every extra krone you earn above NOK 725,050 loses about 43 øre.

Norway PAYE scheme: take-home pay on NOK 600,000 at a flat 25%

This is a foreign worker on the PAYE scheme earning NOK 600,000. The scheme takes a flat 25% of gross pay, which is NOK 150,000, and nothing else, so you keep NOK 450,000, or 75.0% of gross. It works as a final tax, with no allowances or bracket tax to work out.

  1. Gross paya year, before taxNOK 600,000
  2. PAYE scheme (25% of gross, final)tax, taken from pay−NOK 150,000
  3. Take-home pay75.0% of gross, NOK 37,500 a monthNOK 450,000

The flat rate stays 25% at any income up to the NOK 725,050 limit, so it tends to suit higher salaries. Run your own pay both ways in the calculator, and confirm you qualify with Skatteetaten.

How to pay less tax, legally

These are mainstream, legal ways to manage Norwegian tax. Which ones apply depends on your status and income.

Check whether the PAYE scheme beats ordinary tax

Suits: foreign workers who meet the scheme's conditions, especially on higher pay where bracket tax and national insurance add up. Compare your own salary under both regimes, as the 25% flat rate is simple but gives no allowances.

Caveat: the scheme has eligibility rules and a time limit, and you may be unable to claim deductions. Confirm the current conditions with Skatteetaten.

Claim deductions you are entitled to

Suits: residents on ordinary tax. Deductions such as interest on loans and eligible work-related costs reduce the income taxed at 22%. The tax return is pre-filled, so check it and add what is missing.

Caveat: deductions do not reduce bracket tax or national insurance, which are charged on gross pay. The calculator uses only the standard allowances.

Keep your tax card up to date

Suits: anyone with a second job, a change in income or a part-year stay. If your tax card does not reflect your real income, too little tax may be withheld and the gap appears in the following year's tax settlement.

Caveat: updating the card changes withholding only. It does not change your final tax.

Pension saving with a tax deduction

Suits: residents who want to save for retirement. Norway has individual pension savings schemes that give a deduction against ordinary income, within an annual cap.

Caveat: the cap changes, and the money is locked until retirement age. Look up the current limit with Skatteetaten.

What the calculator does not model

  • Employment income only. It models one salary for a full year. It does not cover investment income, capital gains, a business or a part year.
  • Standard rates only. Lower rates in Finnmark and northern Troms, and any items that depend on your municipality, are not modelled.
  • No bonuses or equity. Share options, bonuses and holiday pay are not modelled separately.
  • Flat standard deduction. The calculator applies the minimum standard deduction and the personal allowance, not your real deductions.
  • You choose the regime. The calculator does not test whether you qualify for the PAYE scheme or whether you are a Norwegian tax resident.
  • No wealth tax, no tax treaties. Wealth tax and foreign tax credits are not included.

General information, not tax advice. The figures follow the rules as published for the year shown. Check the ones that matter to you with the tax authority or an adviser before you sign a contract.

Frequently asked questions

How much tax do I pay on NOK 750,000 in Norway?

A resident on ordinary tax pays about NOK 197,000 in income tax, bracket tax and national insurance, and keeps about NOK 553,000. Try your own figure in the Global Income Tax Calculator.

Why is my December pay larger in Norway?

Employers withhold tax over ten and a half months, not twelve. December carries only half the usual deduction, so the payslip is bigger before Christmas, and holiday pay is handled separately. The annual tax is the same either way.

The calculator works out the full-year tax, so a single payslip can differ from it, especially in December.

What is a tax card (skattekort) in Norway?

The tax card tells your employer how much tax to withhold from each payment. Skatteetaten issues it and your employer retrieves it. If your income changes during the year, you can update the card so the withholding fits, and the final tax is settled in your tax return the following spring.

What is trinnskatt and how is it different from the 22% tax?

The 22% tax is charged on ordinary income after deductions. Trinnskatt (bracket tax) is charged on gross personal income with no deductions, in steps from 1.7% up to 17.8%. In the NOK 750,000 example the 22% tax is NOK 118,747 and trinnskatt adds NOK 21,256.

Is the Norwegian PAYE scheme worth it?

It charges a flat 25% of gross and nothing else, with no allowances. On NOK 600,000 that is NOK 150,000. Ordinary tax can come out lower at modest incomes and higher at larger ones, so compare both with your own pay. Eligibility depends on conditions set by Skatteetaten.

Do I pay national insurance on top of income tax?

Yes, employees pay 7.6% national insurance of gross pay once it passes NOK 99,650, phased in above that. It buys membership of the National Insurance Scheme, which covers sickness benefit and pension rights. On the PAYE scheme the flat 25% covers it.
